Also check if there's a way to use VLC as a pure audio player without rendering any video view (since we only need audio playback for OGG files).

Do NOT write any code — just research and report back concisely.

# react-native-vlc-media-player ## Supported RN Versions - 0.59 > 0.62 and up - PODs are updated to work with 0.61 and up (tested in 0.61.5, 0.62 and 0.63) ## Supported formats Support for network streams, RTSP, RTP, RTMP, HLS, MMS. Play all files, [in all formats, including exotic ones, like the classic VLC media player.](#-More-formats) Play MKV, multiple audio tracks (including 5.1), and subtitles tracks (including SSA!) ## Sample repo [VLC Media Player test](https://github.com/razorRun/react-native-vlc-media-player-test) ## Add it to your project Run `npm i react-native-vlc-media-player --save` or `yarn add react-native-vlc-media-player` If not using Expo also run `react-native link react-native-vlc-media-player` ## Android Should work without any specific settings. Gradle build might fail with `More than one file was found with OS independent path 'lib/x86/libc++_shared.so'` error. If that happens, add the following block to your `android/app/build.gradle`: ```gradle tasks.whenTaskAdded((tas -> { // when task is 'mergeLocalDebugNativeLibs' or 'mergeLocalReleaseNativeLibs' if (tas.name.contains("merge") && tas.name.contains("NativeLibs")) { tasks.named(tas.name) {it doFirst { java.nio.file.Path notNeededDirectory = it.externalLibNativeLibs .getFiles() .stream() // for React Native 0.71, the file value now contains "jetified-react-android" instead of "jetified-react-native" .filter(file -> file.toString().contains("jetified-react-native")) .findAny() .orElse(null) .toPath(); java.nio.file.Files.walk(notNeededDirectory).forEach(file -> { if (file.toString().contains("libc++_shared.so")) { java.nio.file.Files.delete(file); } }); } } } })) ``` ### Explanation `react-native` and `LibVLC` both import `libc++_shared.so`, but we cannot use `packagingOptions.pickFirst` to handle this case, because `libvlc-all:3.6.0-eap5` will crash when using `libc++_shared.so`, so we have to use `libc++_shared.so` from `LibVLC`. Reference: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/74258902/how-to-define-which-so-file-to-use-in-gradle-packaging-options ### Also to consider `libvlc-all:3.2.6` has a bug where subtitles won't display on Android 12 and 13, so we have to upgrade `LibVLC` to support it. Reference: https://code.videolan.org/videolan/vlc-android/-/issues/2252 ## iOS 1. cd to ios 2. run `pod init` (if only Podfile has not been generated in ios folder) 3. add `pod 'MobileVLCKit', '3.3.10'` to pod file **(No need if you are running RN 0.61 and up)** 4. run `pod install` (you have to delete the app on the simulator/device and run `react-native run-ios` again) ### Important Starting from iOS 14, you are required to provide a message for the `NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription` key in `Info.plist` if your app uses the local network directly or indirectly. It seems the `MobileVLCKit` library powering the VLC Player on iOS makes use of this feature when playing external media from sources such as RTSP streams from IP cameras. Provide a custom message specifying how your app will make use of the network so your App Store submission is not rejected for this reason, read more about this here: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/bundleresources/information-property-list/nslocalnetworkusagedescription ### Optional In root project select "Build Settings", find "Bitcode" and select "Enable Bitcode" ## Expo This package works with Expo, Expo Go does not include custom native code so you must use a [development build](https://docs.expo.dev/develop/development-builds/introduction/). To enable just insert the `react-native-vlc-media-player` plugin to the "plugins" array from `app.config.js` or `app.json`: ```json { "expo": { "plugins": [ [ "react-native-vlc-media-player", { "ios": { "includeVLCKit": false }, "android": { "legacyJetifier": false } } ] ], } } ``` ### Configuring the plugin is optional: - Set `ios.includeVLCKit` to `true` if using RN < 0.61 - Set `android.legacyJetifier` to `true` if using RN < 0.71 Then rebuild your app as described in the ["Adding custom native code"](https://docs.expo.io/workflow/customizing/) guide. ## Usage ```jsx import { VLCPlayer, VlCPlayerView } from 'react-native-vlc-media-player'; import Orientation from 'react-native-orientation'; // Or you can use {}} /> ``` ### VLCPlayer Props | Prop | Description | Default | | ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- | | `source` | Object that contains the uri of a video or song to play eg `{{ uri: "https://video.com/example.mkv" }}` | `{}` | | `subtitleUri` | local subtitle file path，if you want to hide subtitle, you can set this to an empty subtitle file，current we don't support a `hide subtitle` prop. | | | `paused` | Set to `true` or `false` to pause or play the media | `false` | | `repeat` | Set to `true` or `false` to loop the media | `false` | | `rate` | Set the playback rate of the player | `1` | | `seek` | Set position to seek between `0` and `1` (`0` being the start, `1` being the end , use `position` from the progress object ) | | | `volume` | Set the volume of the player (`number`) | | | `muted` | Set to `true` or `false` to mute the player | `false` | | `audioTrack` | Set audioTrack id (`number`) (see `onLoad` callback VideoInfo.audioTracks) | | | `textTrack` | Set textTrack(subtitle) id (`number`) (see `onLoad` callback- VideoInfo.textTracks) | | | `playInBackground` | Set to `true` or `false` to allow playing in the background | false | | `videoAspectRatio ` | Set the video aspect ratio eg `"16:9"` | | | `autoAspectRatio` | Set to `true` or `false` to enable auto aspect ratio | false | | `resizeMode` | Set the behavior for the video size (`fill, contain, cover, none, scale-down`) | none | | `style` | React native stylesheet styles | `{}` | | `autoplay` | Set to `true` or `false` to enable autoplay | `true` | #### Callback props Callback props take a function that gets fired on various player events: | Prop | Description | | -------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `onPlaying` | Called when media starts playing returns eg `{target: 9, duration: 99750, seekable: true}` | | `onProgress` | Callback containing `position` as a fraction, and `duration`, `currentTime` and `remainingTime` in seconds
  ◦  eg `{ duration: 99750, position: 0.30, currentTime: 30154, remainingTime: -69594 }` | | `onPaused` | Called when media is paused | | `onStopped ` | Called when media is stoped | | `onBuffering ` | Called when media is buffering | | `onEnded` | Called when media playing ends | | `onError` | Called when an error occurs whilst attempting to play media | | `onLoad` | Called when video info is loaded, Callback containing VideoInfo | | `onRecordingCreated` | Called when a new recording is created as the result of `startRecording()` `stopRecording()` | | `onSnapshot` | Called when a new snapshot is created as the result of `snapshot()` - contains `{success: boolean, path?: string, error?: string}` | #### Methods props Methods available on the VLC player ref | Prop | Description | | ----------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `startRecording(directory: string)` | Start recording the current video into the given directory | | `stopRecording()` | Stop recording the current video. The final recording file can be obtained from the `onRecordingCreated` callback | | `snapshot(path: string)` | Capture a snapshot of the current video frame to the given file path | VideoInfo example: ``` { duration: 30906, videoSize: {height: 240, width: 32}, audioTracks: [ {id: -1, name: "Disable"}, {id: 1, name: "Track 1"}, {id: 3, name: "Japanese Audio (2ch LC-AAC) - [Japanese]"} ], textTracks: [ {id: -1, name: "Disable"}, {id: 4, name: "Track 1 - [English]"}, {id: 5, name: "Track 2 - [Japanese]"} ], } ``` ## More formats Container formats: 3GP, ASF, AVI, DVR-MS, FLV, Matroska (MKV), MIDI, QuickTime File Format, MP4, Ogg, OGM, WAV, MPEG-2 (ES, PS, TS, PVA, MP3), AIFF, Raw audio, Raw DV, MXF, VOB, RM, Blu-ray, DVD-Video, VCD, SVCD, CD Audio, DVB, HEIF, AVIF Audio coding formats: AAC, AC3, ALAC, AMR, DTS, DV Audio, XM, FLAC, It, MACE, MOD, Monkey's Audio, MP3, Opus, PLS, QCP, QDM2/QDMC, RealAudio, Speex, Screamtracker 3/S3M, TTA, Vorbis, WavPack, WMA (WMA 1/2, WMA 3 partially). Capture devices: Video4Linux (on Linux), DirectShow (on Windows), Desktop (screencast), Digital TV (DVB-C, DVB-S, DVB-T, DVB-S2, DVB-T2, ATSC, Clear QAM) Network protocols: FTP, HTTP, MMS, RSS/Atom, RTMP, RTP (unicast or multicast), RTSP, UDP, Sat-IP, Smooth Streaming Network streaming formats: Apple HLS, Flash RTMP, MPEG-DASH, MPEG Transport Stream, RTP/RTSP ISMA/3GPP PSS, Windows Media MMS Subtitles: Advanced SubStation Alpha, Closed Captions, DVB, DVD-Video, MPEG-4 Timed Text, MPL2, OGM, SubStation Alpha, SubRip, SVCD, Teletext, Text file, VobSub, WebVTT, TTML Video coding formats: Cinepak, Dirac, DV, H.263, H.264/MPEG-4 AVC, H.265/MPEG HEVC, AV1, HuffYUV, Indeo 3, MJPEG, MPEG-1, MPEG-2, MPEG-4 Part 2, RealVideo 3&4, Sorenson, Theora, VC-1,[h] VP5, VP6, VP8, VP9, DNxHD, ProRes and some WMV. ## Got a few minutes to spare? Please help us to keep this repo up to date and simple to use. #### Our idea was to keep the repo simple, and people can use it with newer RN versions without any additional config. 1. Get a fork of this repo and clone [VLC Media Player test](https://github.com/razorRun/react-native-vlc-media-player-test) 2. Run it for ios and android locally using your fork, and do the changes. (remove this package using `npm remove react-native-vlc-media-player` and install the forked version from git hub `npm i https://git-address-to-your-forked-repo`) 3. Verify your changes and make sure everything works on both platforms. (If you need a hand with testing I might be able to help as well) 4. Send PR. 5. Be happy, Cause you're a Rockstar 🌟 ❤️ ## Known Issues ### iOS 17 Simulator Crash It is a [known issue](https://code.videolan.org/videolan/VLCKit/-/issues/724) that apps can crash on playback in iOS simulator with `EXEC_BAD_ACCESS` errors. This appears to only be on certain iOS 17.x versions (17.4, 17.5). If this happens, try running on an iOS 18+ simulator instead. ## TODO 1. Android video aspect ratio and other params do not work (Events are called but all events come through a single event onVideoStateChange but the JS side does not implement it) ## Credits [cornejobarraza](https://github.com/cornejobarraza) [ammarahm-ed](https://github.com/ammarahm-ed) [Nghi-NV](https://github.com/Nghi-NV) [xuyuanzhou](https://github.com/xuyuanzhou) Author - Roshan Milinda -> [roshan.digital](https://roshan.digital) [result-id: r4] [rerun: b5]

content.content:
# React Native Track Player: Bridgeless Mode Event Issue

Based on the GitHub issue, there is **no TurboModule parsing error**. Instead, the problem involves event emission in bridgeless mode.

## The Issue

In React Native 0.76+ with bridgeless architecture enabled (`newArchEnabled: true`), the `MusicService.emit()` method fails silently. The code hardcodes the legacy pathway:

> "hardcode the legacy `reactNativeHost.reactInstanceManager.currentReactContext` chain to send events to JS"

In bridgeless mode, `currentReactContext` returns `null`, causing all native-to-JavaScript events to be silently dropped without errors or warnings.

## Affected Version

- **React Native**: 0.76+ (New Architecture/bridgeless mode)
- **Specifically tested**: RN 0.81.5 with Expo SDK 54

## The Fix

The solution involves replacing hardcoded legacy paths with the inherited `reactContext` property from `HeadlessJsTaskService`, which correctly handles both bridged and bridgeless architectures:

> "Use the inherited `reactContext` instead of the hardcoded chain in both `emit()` and `emitList()`"

The author confirmed this fix as "Tested and working" and offered to submit a pull request.

---

## Research Report: react-native-vlc-media-player and Alternatives

### 1. react-native-vlc-media-player

**Latest version:** 1.0.98 (published November 28, 2025)

**Actively maintained?** Moderately. Regular releases throughout 2025 (roughly monthly). 445 stars, 217 forks, only 4 open issues. However, the New Architecture support request (issue #253) was closed as "Not planned."

**API surface -- component-based (renders a View):**
- It is a **View-based component** using the old `requireNativeComponent("RCTVLCPlayer")` pattern.
- The underlying iOS native code uses `RCTEventDispatcher` (legacy bridge architecture).

**Playing a local file:**
```jsx
<VLCPlayer source={{ uri: "file:///path/to/file.ogg" }} />
```

**Progress:** `onProgress` callback provides `{ position, duration, currentTime, remainingTime }`

**Pause/Resume:** Declarative via `paused` prop (`true`/`false`), or imperative via ref: `ref.current.resume(true/false)`

**Stop:** `ref.current.stopPlayer()`

**Seek:** `seek` prop (0 to 1 fraction), or `ref.current.seek(pos)`

**OGG support:** Explicitly listed in supported formats (Ogg, Vorbis, Opus -- VLC handles them all natively).

**Audio-only without a video view:** Technically possible by giving the component `style={{ width: 0, height: 0 }}` or wrapping it in a hidden container. The native code manages a "drawable" view, so it's a hack rather than a designed use case. It will work but it's not clean.

### 2. New Architecture / RN 0.80+ Compatibility

**This is the main problem.** `react-native-vlc-media-player` does NOT support the New Architecture:
- Uses `requireNativeComponent` (Old Architecture / Paper)
- iOS native code uses `RCTEventDispatcher` (legacy bridge)
- Issue #253 requesting New Architecture support was closed as "Not planned"
- No Fabric or TurboModule code exists in the repo

Since your project has New Architecture enabled (`RCTNewArchEnabled`), this library will only work via the **interop layer** (Old Architecture compatibility mode that RN provides). This may work but is fragile and not guaranteed long-term. There could be subtle issues with event delivery or view lifecycle.

### 3. Alternatives Evaluated

**react-native-vlcplayer-2:** Does not exist on npm. Not a real package.

**react-native-track-player (v4.1.2, v5.0.0-alpha0)**
- **Pros:** Purely imperative API (no View needed), 3.7k stars, uses Media3/ExoPlayer on Android (OGG works natively), has React hooks (`useProgress`, `usePlaybackState`), background playback, lock screen controls, queue management.
- **Cons:** iOS uses AVPlayer which does NOT natively support OGG/Vorbis (only AAC, MP3, ALAC, WAV, AIFF). New Architecture support is **in progress but unstable** -- `MusicService.emit()` is broken in bridgeless mode (events silently dropped). A fix exists but hasn't been merged into a stable release yet. The v5.0.0-alpha0 targets New Arch but is alpha.
- **OGG on iOS: BLOCKING ISSUE.** AVPlayer cannot decode OGG/Vorbis or OGG/Opus natively. You would need to transcode or use a custom decoder.

**react-native-audio-api (v0.11.7, Software Mansion)**
- **Pros:** Very actively maintained (855 commits, 735 stars), explicitly supports OGG/Opus decoding (added in v0.8.0), from a reputable maintainer (Software Mansion).
- **Cons:** This is a **low-level Web Audio API** port, not a simple media player. Playing a file requires constructing an audio graph (AudioContext, AudioBufferSourceNode, etc.). No built-in progress callback -- you'd need to track it yourself. The "simple playback" (Audio tag) feature is on their roadmap but not yet released.

**react-native-sound (v0.13.0)**
- Simple imperative API, but no OGG support on iOS (uses AVAudioPlayer). Last meaningful update was 2025. No New Architecture support.

**expo-av (v16.0.8)**
- Expo's audio/video module. Uses AVPlayer on iOS, so same OGG limitation. Requires Expo modules infrastructure.

### 4. Recommendation Summary

| Library | OGG Support | New Arch | Audio-only (no View) | Maintenance |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| react-native-vlc-media-player | Yes (both platforms) | No (interop only) | Hack (zero-size View) | Moderate |
| react-native-track-player | Android yes, iOS NO | Unstable/alpha | Yes (imperative) | Active |
| react-native-audio-api | Yes (both platforms) | Unknown/likely | Yes (imperative) | Very active |
| react-native-sound | Android yes, iOS NO | No | Yes (imperative) | Low |

**For OGG playback specifically**, your realistic options are:

1. **react-native-vlc-media-player** via the interop layer -- works today, OGG on both platforms, but technically debt since it doesn't support New Arch and the maintainer has no plans to add it. Use a zero-size View for audio-only.

2. **react-native-audio-api** -- supports OGG on both platforms natively, from Software Mansion (high quality), but requires writing Web Audio API-style code (AudioContext graph) rather than a simple "play this file" call. More effort to integrate but more future-proof.

3. **Transcode OGG to a supported format** (e.g., AAC/M4A) before playback, then use `react-native-track-player` which has the cleanest imperative API. This adds complexity but sidesteps the codec problem entirely.
